newsitem.title: CANADA: US court lets Novopharm sell generic Zantac - company.
newsitem.headline: US court lets Novopharm sell generic Zantac - company.

text.p: A U.S. court has cleared the way for Novopharm Ltd to produce a generic drug of the ulcer drug Glaxo Wellcome Plc's popular ulcer drug Zantac, Novopharm said on Sunday.
The privately-held Scarborough, Ontario, company said the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit had made the ruling on Friday and its generic version would be in pharmacies in July.
It said Zantac, generically called ranitidine hydrochloride, was the world's best selling prescription medication, with estimated U.S. sales of US$1.63 billion.

"Novopharm is the only company that has successfully navigated through the complex litigation process and is now able to produce a generic ranitidine (Zantac)," Novopharm Chairman and Chief Executive Leslie Dan stated.

A Novopharm statement said: "In their efforts to prevent a generic version of their drug from entering the market, Glaxo Wellcome has repeatedly claimed in court that producing Form 1 ranitidine will infringe on their Form 2 patent.

"Glaxo presently holds two patents on ranitidine: Form 1, which would have expired in December 1995 if not for the 20- month patent extension given to them under the GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade) legislation and Form 2, expiring in 2002."
It said Form 1 and Form 2 were therapeutically equivalent.

Dan added: "The Federal Courts have made it very clear that any manufacturer looking to make a generic version of Zantac must prove in court that they are making a pure version of Form 1 ranitidine, and not a mixture of Form 1 and Form 2. Novopharm has clearly proven this in the courts."
It said the Appeals Court affirmed the district court's ruling that "Glaxo failed to prove infringement by a preponderance of the evidence."

Last July, it said, a federal judge had sided with Novopharm in a verdict that stated "Glaxo has failed to establish that the existence of Form 2 in Novopharm's product is even a reasonable possibility."
Dan said the patent for Zantac would expire on July 25. "With this behind us, Novopharm is moving full speed ahead towards bringing a generic version of Zantac to the market," he said.

Novopharm has also received, the statement said, a tentative Abbreviated New Drug Application from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for a generic version of Glaxo Wellcome's Zovirax (acyclovir) and plans to market the product on April 23 following patent expiration. It said acyclovir has U.S. sales of $488 million.
Novopharm Ltd is the parent of Novopharm Biotech Inc, which is not involved with generic versions of Zantac or Zovirax, a spokeswoman said.
